statement: Where area-based structures report upward through a separate operational cell rather than to the cluster, the same needs information travels up and back down again, looping between two parallel structures.
quote: It started down there, going up, then I have to take it back again, take it down there. So we are in some form of a loop.

statement: Cluster coordinators are not permitted to engage directly with area-based structures and must route all contact through an intermediary operational cell.
quote: You cannot engage with ABC as clusters. If you need to engage with ABC as cluster, you have to go through us as the operational cell.

statement: Subnational cluster coordinators may attend area-based coordination meetings only if invited, leaving the cluster with no standing presence at district level.
quote: can my subnational cluster be part of the ABC coordination forum or the coordination meetings? They say, no, they can be invited if the ABC needs them to be there. So at the moment, that is the kind of the dynamic that is existing.

statement: Area-based structures were established in roughly fifteen of twenty-one prioritised districts, leaving part of the prioritised caseload outside the new architecture.
quote: the ABC is at district level and then currently it is designed along the 21 hyper-prioritized districts… But even at this point, so far, it is only 14 or 15 out of the 21 districts have the ABCs in place.

statement: Area-based coordination facilitators double-hat and are incentivised by their host organisations, so the structure runs on borrowed capacity rather than dedicated posts.
quote: this lead and the colleague, the leaders or facilitators, the co-facilitators, are double-hatting and incentivized by the organizations that are hosting these facilitators or the co-facilitators of the ABC

statement: Area-based coordination was introduced to counterbalance a coordination architecture perceived as UN-centred and out of touch with international and national NGOs and with communities at district level.
quote: they feel this axis is more of a heavy UN centred structure in place. So what they seem to have introduced with the ABC coordination system is that they try to bring a more balanced approach to this and to be more in touch with the fact that the clusters are not in touch with the [community] at the district level

statement: For the 2027 planning cycle strategic objectives, severity and PIN analysis and budgeting were retained nationally, while needs contextualisation, response design and prioritisation moved to area-based forums.
quote: in terms of the HNRP, what they maintained at the national level [is] that we'll be doing the strategic objectives. We'll maintain the strategic objective at national level. And then the [JIAF] analysis for the PIN and severity, that one still remains at the national level. And then financial requirements, doing the budgeting for the clusters, that one has been retained at the national level. What is decentralized to area-based level is the contextualization of the needs.

statement: Pooled fund prioritisation moved to area-based structures, with the cluster's contribution concentrated at technical review of proposals.
quote: these needs or meetings or prioritization will take place within the ABCs… they are going to have a discussion with the ABCs in terms of this allocation and when the ABCs will prioritize the activities, the ABC will prioritize which location, which venue and all that

statement: Clusters were asked to select priority districts from a pre-approved list, which left little room to propose alternatives based on access or observed need.
quote: So what you are asking us is just to rubber stamp what you have already agreed. Is it just to rubber stamp, or are we here to give our constructive input?

statement: The cluster first saw the pooled fund allocation strategy when a partner forwarded it, rather than receiving it through the coordination channels.
quote: At this point, as of last week, they have already drafted the standard allocation strategy for their location. Personally, none of us have seen it. I'm getting this information from the partners… I'm only seeing the strategy as of last week because it was shared to me by a partner.

statement: Subnational cluster coordinators were approached directly for allocation input without the national coordinator included, which made it harder for the cluster to present a single position.
quote: They did ask us for the contact of the sub-national cluster coordinators. The sub-national coordinators shared the list of WASH activities that they want them incorporated. They did not ask us, they did not even put us in copy that this communication has been sent to the sub-national. So we are completely blank or blind on that.

statement: Withdrawal of a major bilateral donor triggered a reprioritisation cutting prioritised districts from sixty-five to twenty-one, which then set the geographic scope of area-based coordination.
quote: with the withdrawal of the funding from the BHA or from the USAID, then there was a second level of reprioritization that was done. And this reduced the districts from 65 to 21.

statement: Subnational coordination posts funded through lead agency partnership agreements are not being renewed, putting dedicated subnational capacity at risk just as the architecture is being redesigned.
quote: you were mentioning those PCAs with some of the subnational focal points… we might be able to have a little bit of support financially to coordination capacities in some of the priority countries and Somalia will be one of [them]

statement: The cluster lead agency signalled an eventual handover of coordination to the line ministry without setting a timeline, prompting early informal engagement rather than a planned process.
quote: He was not so sure of the timeline, but it is in the horizon.

statement: Joint agenda setting with the line ministry and inviting ministry representatives to chair national coordination meetings moved government participation beyond opening and closing formalities.
quote: When I'm setting up meetings for the national clusters, I ensure that we have the conversation, agree on the date, joint agenda setting if they have anything specifically they want to put in there… I'm also moving beyond them just opening the meetings and closing the meetings. I've requested that from time to time they can actively be the chair of these national coordination meetings.

statement: The cluster began channelling humanitarian WASH information into the line ministry's development coordination platform to build a nexus link ahead of transition.
quote: I'm also linking up the cluster from the humanitarian side with the development platform for WASH for development. There is a platform at the ministry of energy and water resource to see how whatever information is at the humanitarian level, how can it be fed to this development platform… the spirit of the development nexus.

statement: Ministry counterparts were initially hesitant about taking on coordination responsibility because they expected an imminent transfer; framing transition as a phased process rather than a handover date reduced that hesitancy.
quote: Initially they felt, are you going to tell us to do it next month? I said no, it is a process.

statement: State-level ministry engagement varies widely within one country, with some convening and documenting coordination meetings and others not, so transition readiness is uneven below national level.
quote: At state level, some of the nine ministries are quite very, very strong and they do take the lead in meetings, or the monthly meetings. They also call for the quarterly meetings, and even they do share the minutes, they do share the list of the partners and the activities they are doing.

statement: A ministry focal point who had previously attended cluster coordination training understood cluster functions well, which made early transition discussions substantially easier.
quote: one thing I appreciate with the focal point person is that he has [been] made to attend a number of the cluster coordination workshop or training. He has a very good understanding of the cluster functions… he really does understand it, which is a positive thing.

statement: Government counterparts asked to learn directly from countries where coordination has already transitioned to government, rather than receiving guidance material alone.
quote: They were asking if they can have some lessons learned, to visit other contexts where the transition has happened.

statement: An incoming cluster coordinator received no handover report and had to reconstruct institutional knowledge unaided from shared drives, losing time to work already done.
quote: I've been going through the available products, available information within the system itself, between my predecessor and also the current co-coordinator, to see whether there was any handing over report that was done… I reached personally to my predecessor, I think, two, three times. He said he'll be available, but on the material day, he could not show up… So I decided just to go through the Google Drive myself, got the access, looked at what information are available there.

statement: Information management recruitment was cancelled and the post downgraded to a volunteer position on cost grounds, leaving the cluster without dedicated information management capacity.
quote: At the time when I joined, they were doing the recruitment of the information management officer. And it was going on well until again it stopped. And then they are saying they are looking for UNV instead of NOB. So now they are looking for UNV.

statement: Public cluster dashboards and contact details went unupdated for months while partner reporting continued to arrive, indicating the constraint is analytical capacity rather than data availability.
quote: It is not that there is no information. This data is available. Partners do send us every month.

statement: Partners continued to report response data through the cluster 4W only, with area-based structures collecting assessment and prioritisation information but not response reporting, so the parallel structures did not create double reporting.
quote: The ABC mostly they do collect, they do assessments or when it comes to the prioritization of villages or needs, which one can be prioritized. But in terms of the reporting, partner at the moment, we have maintained the reporting through the 4W still.

statement: After eight years with the same co-coordinating agency the cluster opened a competitive expression of interest to rotate the role, while considering retaining the outgoing agency in a roving support function.
quote: I wanted to know if there are any experience in terms of calling for the expression of interest or any sample of such kind of announcements or inviting the partners, how to go about vetting for a co-coordinating organisation. I know there is the process of having an MOU or an LOU…

statement: Resistance to area-based coordination reflects how it was introduced rather than the concept itself, since community consultation and needs prioritisation were already standard practice among partners.
quote: The idea behind ABC, for me it is a good one, having that link with the community. That is what has always been there. It is not a new concept. Maybe the way it is being brought about is the problem.

statement: Cluster coordinators asked for structured exchange with counterparts in other countries running area-based structures, to understand how the cluster-ABC relationship works elsewhere before redesigning their own.
quote: I really want to understand how the ABC is engaging with the cluster in those other contexts or in other countries.

statement: Subnational clusters were redefined as technical advisers to area structures and barred from holding routine standing meetings, restricting them to ad hoc topic-specific gatherings.
quote: They cannot have routine standing meetings with a full group of people. They can only have ad hoc targeted meetings.

statement: A zonal coordination layer chaired by the humanitarian coordination office replaced the subnational intersectoral tier, with clusters positioned as technical advisers to it.
quote: at sub-national level here, they say no more clusters, but we only have the zonal groups, which are sort of replacing the… ICCG… And the cluster, the sub-national clusters are technical focal points or technical advisors, depending on the paper you look at… you have the zonal CGs, coordination groups, and that's chaired by OCHA

statement: All eleven area-based structures are chaired by local actors, placing national organisations formally at the head of district-level coordination.
quote: we have 11 ABCs, and they are chaired by local actors, which is great so far

statement: Paid area coordinator posts were created alongside the elected chairs and co-chairs, with job descriptions drafted centrally, which leaves the role of the elected leadership unclear.
quote: The chair and co-chair will become quite meaningless in terms of roles and responsibilities. It is a bit of cosmetic stuff.

statement: Every area coordinator post across all eleven structures was awarded to one national NGO that is the nationalised affiliate of an international confederation, which raises a question about how localisation is defined in practice.
quote: they are hiring ABC coordinators… it's going to be paid by the humanitarian fund… so far they have 8 coordinators hired in those 11 ABCs… so you have three people, you have a coordinator and then you have chair and co-chair. So the problem is the chair and co-chair will become quite meaningless in terms of roles and responsibilities… it's all from the same organization, which is not really what we like.

statement: The area coordinator arrangement was not set out in published guidance, and the cluster learned of it informally before seeking confirmation.
quote: that is in no guidance. I figured it out via… and then I asked OCHA, they were like, oh yeah, sorry, it's because it's new.

statement: With operational gap analysis moved off subnational platforms, no forum currently holds it during sudden emergencies, when partners need to know who is working where rather than which technical standard applies.
quote: When there is a massive displacement you go for an emergency, you do not care about the design of the latrine.

statement: Information flow between area structures, subnational clusters and the intersectoral group is not yet defined, so the same information is requested in both directions and roles remain unsettled.
quote: Even the ICCG is asking us to give information about ABC or partner presence. We are like, it is not your job now. So it is very confusing.

statement: Escalation pathways between area, subnational and national levels are not described in the terms of reference of the new structures.
quote: the clusters TOR need to change, right? Because it's not massive, but in terms of relationships and especially escalation pathway. That's not very well described. And the other major issue we have is information flow. That is absolutely not explicit.

statement: Ambiguity about the new structure caused a double-hatting subnational focal point to stop convening partners altogether, including during an emergency, until the cluster clarified that he still could.
quote: the Southeast Wash person who's double hatting — he didn't think he could have meetings anymore. And when we had an emergency, he wasn't dealing with that. He was just dealing with [agency] partners. That's a massive problem, right? So now we've established that it's okay.

statement: Partners in one area formally demanded that the previous subnational cluster arrangement be retained, and it was kept in place pending a decision.
quote: there's even an area where partners demanded to keep it as before. So they are keeping it. For now, but until OCHA says no.

statement: Final versions of the national area-coordination guidance were not held by the cluster lead agency, and the cluster had to assemble a comparison against global guidance itself to establish what applied.
quote: Nobody knew what their name was anymore.

statement: A simple partner presence and gap analysis tool built by the cluster for area structures was well received, indicating demand for cluster technical support rather than rejection of the cluster role.
quote: here we had a cluster coordinator who explicitly drafted a tool for the ABC so they could do a [partner] gap analysis, you know, for the emergencies. And they were like very pleased, but it's just one tool made in an hour by a specialized staff

statement: The area-based architecture is presented as a permanent replacement rather than a transitional arrangement, which changes what is at stake in getting the design right.
quote: It is not transitional. I thought it was transitional. It is not transitional, it is permanent.

statement: Area structures take part in two rounds of consultation on severity scoring and may override the calculated score with local expert judgement, giving them real influence over the analysis.
quote: this round here, there are two rounds of ABC consultation. So we have three or four draft pins that will go back and forth… and ABCs will always have this, like, can override [the] expert with their expert judgment on the severity score of an area if they don't agree

statement: Severity scores are computed centrally across clusters and returned to area level only for validation, with the cluster not involved in designing the indicators that feed them.
quote: It's managed by OCHA… we will come up with scores. OCHA will compute scores, looking at 4 clusters, having the same [criteria]… and then that score will go back to ABC level, to area level, and then they'll say, yes, this is a three, no, that's not a three, it's a four, based on qualitative expertise. That's all we know so far. It's never been done.

statement: WASH was not prioritised in a pooled fund localisation allocation, obliging the cluster to lobby partners to embed WASH activities inside other sectors proposals.
quote: We have the MHF right now, Myanmar Humanitarian Fund. It's localization allocation, 15 million. WASH is not prioritized, so I called everybody and their mother to add WASH in the proposal, for integration with education, protection, gender, et cetera.

statement: Local NGOs were added to a proposal review committee that had been composed only of international organisations, at the cluster's insistence.
quote: we have 6 reviewers for the WASH cluster of NGOs. I managed to have local NGOs added because it was only internationals.

statement: Subnational coordination capacity was retained through double-hatting arrangements in all but two areas, so the structure survived without dedicated posts.
quote: sub-national capacity is still there… We have double hatters everywhere except [two areas]. And no, they are still there. They're super good, active.

statement: The response plan scope excludes the recurrent hazard the cluster is actually responding to, on the grounds that it is seasonal and long-standing, leaving live operations outside the planning framework.
quote: We do not have flood in the HPC, but the only thing I am responding to since I am here is floods.

statement: National and global guidance were interpreted differently on whether sectors may choose their own severity methodology, leaving the cluster unable to confirm what was permitted.
quote: the guidance says that sectors could use any methodology they want. Do you confirm?… because in Myanmar, they're applying the last year guidance saying it should be derived from multi-sectoral evidence-based assessment, aka MSNA… so anyways, it seems that we can, despite what they were saying. I think it was just the way it was phrased.

statement: The teams producing vulnerability and exposure analysis do not work on response planning, so their products are not designed for the planning process they are being asked to feed.
quote: The challenge I think is just that [the WIA] team don't do HNRPs. And so I would say if you're experimenting with using the WIA for the HNRP, involve [the coordination side] in that experimentation. I wouldn't leave it just to [that] team because they don't know what it's feeding into.

statement: Almost no partner assessments were shared with the cluster despite repeated requests, leaving very little material for a secondary data review.
quote: On the SDR, we have zero partners assessment, very little. We asked for it, so we'll keep bringing in, calling, collecting them. We can't run them on the AI because of data confidentiality unless we anonymize them… otherwise we have not done an SDR in Myanmar in the previous years.

statement: Partner assessments cannot be processed with AI tools without anonymisation first, because of data confidentiality obligations the cluster is unwilling to breach.
quote: We cannot run them on the AI because of data confidentiality unless we anonymise them.

statement: An information sharing protocol required clusters to classify their products by sensitivity, and the exercise found sensitive material openly accessible on a shared drive.
quote: the information sharing protocol… they're asking clusters to have some discussions, a workshop with the partners to classify what's what… National clusters will establish common [use] cases and standards for the respective sectors, and then each organization should classify as well… I found three sensitive [items]. We're going to have a public folder, restricted on Google Drive with a password just for us, and then confidential is going to be on [agency] SharePoint only.

statement: Sensitivity classification is harder for WASH than for other sectors because infrastructure locations and chemical stocks carry dual-use risk in a conflict setting.
quote: People are telling me that for WASH it is more difficult than for education, because that is just books.

statement: Sub-national level data on violations is published openly on an external platform outside any cluster control, and cross-border information about the country cannot be governed by the in-country protocol at all.
quote: the MRM, this IHL violation tracking — it's actually public on the MRM website and there's a lot of Myanmar Township level data there. So I flagged that as well, but that needs attention too… also what about the cross-border information, what comes out about Myanmar, we don't have control over that.

statement: A partner capacity building programme committed the cluster to fund, facilitate and deliver every requested training, scheduled across the planning peak, until the coordinator intervened to postpone it.
quote: they did a needs assessment, like capacity building needs assessment for all partners, like what do you need — and the Wash cluster… they committed to actually provide all the trainings, pay for all of them, facilitate all of them. So she was gone like for five weeks if I had not intervened during the HPC… she had planned all the trainings in October during the PIN [and severity] calculations. So I told her to postpone to January.

statement: The strategic advisory group had not met for eighteen months, leaving decisions to coordinators alone, and an earlier attempt to recruit a co-coordinator from local actors was abandoned.
quote: it hasn't been meeting for a year and a half… they haven't had a SAG meeting, so all decisions were taken by coordinators

notes: Underpinning evidence, Section 5 of the Transition SDR. Grounded in the S1-S31 evidence base.

statement: Assess and build capacity at national and subnational level before handover, anchored institutionally rather than in individuals.
notes: Underpinning evidence, Section 5 of the Transition SDR. Grounded in the S1-S31 evidence base.

statement: Retain technical standards custody, analysis, partner mapping, risk analysis and provider of last resort in explicit successor arrangements.
notes: Underpinning evidence, Section 5 of the Transition SDR. Grounded in the S1-S31 evidence base.

notes: SDR-level synthesis. Not independent of the sources it synthesises.

notes: SDR-level synthesis. Not independent of the sources it synthesises.

statement: The entire counterpart team at the lead ministry changed within one year, including at senior level, leaving nobody the cluster had previously worked with; meetings to rebuild the relationship did not take place and the transition dialogue stalled.
quote: el equipo de la institucionalidad, que era en este caso el del viceministerio de agua y saneamiento, con el cual se había adelantado todos los procesos… Por temas administrativos y demás salió todo el equipo. O sea, no quedó ni una de las personas con las cuales teníamos ese trabajo en conjunto. Eso implicó que también hubiera nuevos intentos, porque también hubo cambio de viceministra

statement: The cluster has had no dedicated information management post this year, having previously been supported both by the refugee coordination platform and directly by the lead agency, and now relies on intermittent consortium and consultancy support.
notes: Extracted from Colombia country consultation (Spanish). | UNVERIFIED 2026-08: quote backfill found nothing supporting 'no dedicated IM post this year, having previously been supported both by the refugee coordination platform and...'. The transcript discusses IM support being provided, not withdrawn. Third record of this kind after HTI E0513 and SDN E0429. Check against the recording or delete.

statement: Clusters had limited involvement in the first pooled fund allocation, and the indicator list issued to partners diverged from the indicators agreed in the sector operational framework.
quote: dentro del listado de indicadores que ponían a los socios había unos indicadores que eran muy alejados de los indicadores que se habían acordado en el marco operativo

statement: An inventory of the information assets the cluster holds was compiled as part of transition planning, so that products can be summarised and taken on by government entities.
quote: ya igual también estamos haciendo ese inventario de los recursos que tenemos, porque en el momento de la transición con la entidad de gobierno también se busca que sean resumidos y gestionados

statement: A costed transfer plan was prepared with a risk analysis and an inventory of information resources, to be validated by the humanitarian coordinator, and deliberately framed as a transition rather than a deactivation.
quote: elaboramos un plan de transferencia… Entonces ese documento como tal ya está, incluso con análisis de riesgos, con un inventario también de los recursos de información que tenemos.

statement: Transition preparation began with a documentation exercise reconstructing how the cluster was formed and how earlier transitions went, combined with a partner survey on expectations and recommendations.
quote: desde el segundo semestre empezamos a hacer unos procesos, primero de recuento, de recopilación de toda la memoria de cómo había nacido el cluster y las transiciones y demás, y también hicimos una encuesta con los socios para reconocer cuáles eran sus perspectivas, cuáles eran sus recomendaciones

statement: When the regulatory water ministry proved not to be operational during emergencies, the cluster shifted its transition counterpart to the health ministry, which works directly with municipalities on water quality, vector control, sanitation and hygiene.
quote: como estrategia buscamos ese acercamiento con el Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, teniendo en cuenta que en las emergencias el Viceministerio de Agua no es una entidad operativa, es más una entidad rectora, pero en las emergencias el Ministerio de Salud…

statement: The proposed successor is a specialised technical roundtable inside an existing inter-institutional environmental health commission, which already brings together the water ministry, the health ministry and national research institutes, serving as both an operational and an advisory body.
quote: en Colombia, desde varios años hay algo que se llama la Comisión Nacional de Salud Ambiental… Entonces lo que buscamos es que el cluster como tal pueda transicionar hacia una mesa técnica especializada de la Conasa.

statement: A change of national government froze transition dialogues, with the incoming administration signalling a reduction in the number of government entities and its position on humanitarian cooperation not yet known.
quote: el mes de junio ya fue cambio de gobierno y el gobierno electo es un gobierno no oficialista, es un gobierno de oposición… Entonces hasta ahí quedaron congeladas las reuniones, porque todo está muy en términos de cuál va a ser el nuevo interés y la nueva posición que va a tener el nuevo gobierno.

statement: The cluster set three explicit conditions for its position that it should transition rather than deactivate: humanitarian needs have worsened rather than improved, government capacity that is strong nationally is not matched at territorial level where recurrent emergencies overwhelm resources, and needs persist.
quote: algo que hay que dejar muy claro es que el cluster Wash de Colombia no se desactiva, sino que entiende o da una transición teniendo 3 cosas, digamos, o 3 principios

statement: The separate refugee and migrant response plan is being discontinued and merged into a single response plan, with refugees and migrants included only where they intend to remain, and no regional refugee plan will follow.
quote: ya no va a haber plan de respuesta para refugiados inmigrantes. O sea, a partir del otro año los 2 planes se unifican en uno solo, que es el HRP.

statement: A short implementation window of four to six months led almost all partners to prioritise distribution of critical supplies over rehabilitation or system improvement, because longer works were not feasible in the time available.
quote: son implementaciones rápidas que se pensaron para 6 meses… serán casi cuatro meses de implementación

statement: A twelve-month implementation window in the next funding round is expected to allow more integrated work and sustained presence rather than rapid distribution.
quote: los próximos fondos van a tener un tiempo de implementación de 12 meses, lo cual permite acciones mucho más integrales, incluso con mayor presencia

statement: Clusters were consulted in the second allocation round, asked to submit a matrix recommending municipalities together with substantive observations, after having raised the omission from the first round.
quote: en esta segunda asignación, por lo menos a los clusters nos tuvieran en cuenta y por ejemplo nos solicitaron una matriz donde además de decir qué municipios…

statement: Life-saving criteria should extend beyond supply distribution to include contributions to protective environments — water and sanitation in schools, shelters and temporary accommodation — so that funded actions are intersectoral rather than dispersed.
quote: el donante pasó un listado de actividades en el marco de salvar vidas y en ese marco de actividades, cuando los socios seleccionan… Los sectores que se priorizaron, marco de salvar vidas, efectivamente fue Wash.

statement: The cluster recommended including municipalities at the second-highest severity level where armed conflict had recently intensified or where gaps in child health and preventable mortality persisted, rather than restricting allocations to the highest severity band alone.
quote: consideramos aquellos municipios que están en severidad cuatro, pero también aquellos que de pronto están en severidad 3

statement: Rapid entries into and exits from communities, driven by the need to reach the highest-severity municipalities within a short window, carry a risk of unintended harm — a point the cluster raised with the donor.
quote: Muchos socios tratando de focalizar comunidades dentro de los municipios que estaban con severidad cuatro, pero al final esas entradas y salidas rápidas del territorio también pueden generar un riesgo en términos de acción con daño.

statement: Partners reported instances of infant formula being distributed without complementary water and sanitation activities, which reduces the benefit of the nutrition intervention and can introduce health risk.
quote: me reportaron los socios que habían colegas de nutrición que estaban entregando leche en polvo sin acciones complementarias de Wash, que puede ser una acción con riesgo

statement: Armed group control of territory confines communities and restricts movement, cutting access to rivers and water sources and forcing reliance on unsafe storage, with documented increases in infectious disease; indigenous and Afro-descendant communities in the Pacific region are the most affected.
quote: Cuando hay esos confinamientos o restricciones a la movilidad, el acceso a servicios es crítico.

statement: The main humanitarian donor for the sector prioritises protection, health and education, funding very little WASH directly and concentrating instead on intersectoral coordination and information.
quote: como Eco, priorizan sectores como protección, salud y educación en emergencias

statement: Multi-sector needs assessment has not been run for around three years because the country has substantial official data, and the sector calculation does not rely on it.
quote: Colombia en realidad lleva hace como unos 3 años que no se aplica la MSNA y en realidad cuando se aplicaba, dado que es un país que tiene bastantes datos oficiales, no era muy útil.

statement: The cluster must now produce the refugee and migrant disaggregation itself, a function previously carried by the separate refugee coordination platform, without additional capacity.
quote: este año tenemos que tener la desagregación de refugiados inmigrantes… Ahora es ver qué información logramos tener para este otro cálculo o desagregación de refugiados inmigrantes.

statement: Data needed to estimate refugee and migrant needs sits in a national government social registry that the cluster has found difficult to obtain access to.
quote: esta información la estamos intentando sacar de una fuente que se llama el Sisbén. El Sisbén es la forma en cómo se contabiliza por parte del gobierno nacional… las necesidades y las afectaciones de aquellas personas que no tienen acceso a ningún tipo de atención.

statement: The cluster documents its severity and needs methodology and publishes it openly alongside the results, so the basis of the calculation is available to anyone who questions it.
quote: Seguimos manejando la misma metodología que en los años anteriores… siempre la documentamos, incluso la subimos a ReliefWeb también para que ahí quede de soporte.

statement: A partner agency questioned the sector needs methodology across several clusters, disagreeing with how the calculation was done.
quote: la representación de WFP nos hizo varios cuestionamientos, no solo a nosotros, sino a varios cluster sobre la metodología, porque no estaban de acuerdo en el cálculo de la metodología
notes: Extracted from Colombia country consultation (Spanish). | CORRECTED 2026-08: the statement previously read '...as reflecting poverty rather than humanitarian need'. No passage supports that characterisation; the source records disagreement with the calculation only. Clause removed.

statement: Strong working relationships with the protection and shelter clusters allow WASH to be positioned as an enabling sector for others, which matters where the crisis is characterised primarily as a protection crisis.
quote: en Colombia tenemos un buen relacionamiento con los cluster que son estratégicos, o sea, con protección somos partner. De hecho, hemos coincidido en muchas observaciones de cómo Wash puede ser un sector habilitante de otro sector.

statement: Temporary accommodation is set up quickly under national disaster arrangements, and gender and child-specific considerations, along with shelter and WASH standards, are not always applied consistently.
quote: los grupos de trabajo o las áreas de responsabilidad, por ejemplo temas de género, temas de todo lo que es salud sexual y reproductiva, se han visto desfinanciadas y se han visto duramente golpeadas

statement: Gender and sexual and reproductive health areas of responsibility have been heavily defunded, and education was excluded from both allocation rounds on the grounds that its activities are not life-saving.
quote: los grupos de trabajo o las áreas de responsabilidad, por ejemplo temas de género, temas de todo lo que es salud sexual y reproductiva, se han visto desfinanciadas y se han visto duramente golpeadas

statement: Where a technical study would document vulnerability publicly, its timing should be agreed with the incoming government first, since publishing during a change of administration can undermine the transition relationship it is meant to support.
quote: …un estudio técnico aparezca diciendo que hay esta vulnerabilidad sin previamente haber concertado con este gobierno que entra, sería como mi sugerencia

statement: All eighteen state cluster coordinator posts are filled by double-hatting staff, in several cases alongside an NGO co-coordinator, so subnational coordination runs entirely on borrowed capacity.
quote: all 18 states are either having double-hatting coordinator or… And sometimes they're having double hatting as well as the cluster, the NGO co-coordinator, especially in Darfur and some of the critical areas

statement: The second coordination post is a temporary appointment unlikely to survive the current budget review, leaving no certainty that two coordination positions exist next year.
quote: currently there is a PBR going on in the office. We didn't discuss it, but the likelihood of my position to remain is very low. So it's not something we know.

statement: A national co-coordinator drawn from a Sudanese NGO supports the team, and a second is planned, both to ease workload and to give local NGOs a national counterpart they can approach directly.
quote: We were having a co-cluster coordinator from the country itself, a national Sudanese co-coordinator to support us from one of the NGOs. We are going to again talk about it and we're going to try and have one more co-coordinator in the days to come, so that at least it can ease up our job… it's more like a good feel for the local NGOs that they have someone who they can talk to

statement: Vulnerability analysis presented previously was not taken up by partners: the framework was not widely understood, and what it prioritised did not always match what partners observed in the field.
quote: the WIA was already presented in the past, but because, again, of the quality of the data and maybe the methodology of the WIA, it was not picked by partners because it didn't speak to them

statement: A new central planning and reporting platform is being introduced alongside the cluster's existing reporting system, which would leave partners entering the same activity in both.
quote: as you already aware of this new HPC tool… this is in this month, so the middle of the year, and then it's like starting the plan from the middle of the year

statement: State-level expert judgement is built into the severity and needs analysis alongside the survey results, because data quality and the pace of change make survey data alone unreliable and the eighteen state coordination platforms hold genuine field knowledge.
quote: we are doing an expert judgment consultation that will include severity and include the WIA… because in Sudan you cannot go without it because of the quality of the data and the change of the situation. But in addition to that, our state coordination platform are very strong. So they really have expert judgment.

statement: Running the expert judgement exercise as a single process covering needs figures, vulnerability analysis and planning together engages state coordinators in the analysis rather than presenting them with a finished product.
quote: it's also allow us to engage everybody for the pin, for the WIA, for the planification. So it's not going to be WIA expert judgments, it's going to be pin, WIA and planification. Because we have 18 states, you know, here.

statement: An assessment of more than sixteen hundred water points, heading toward twenty-two hundred, was presented to a government-development water task force with an accompanying dashboard.
quote: Today presented to the Water Task Force, which is a development, the water facility mapping that is leading in Khartoum… is the assessment of more than 1600 boards and is going to finalize 2200 by the end of August with a dashboard

statement: Facility and asset mapping is among the most effective bridges to development actors, because it produces something they need and creates a shared table where sector coordination otherwise has none.
quote: presented to the Water Task Force, which is a sector, which is a development, the water facility mapping that is leading in Khartoum

statement: Recruiting state-level information management support has stalled, with previous surge deployments and overall coordination staffing levels both weighing on the decision.
quote: in IM, there have been discussion in the office to get support for the IM officer on state level coordination, state level IM. Not national level, state level, but… The office has been quite reluctant with our past.

statement: The profile needed for state-level information management is hard to fill because the work is not a short emergency deployment: it connects to systems transitioning and to how the cluster will function in future, so it needs someone embedded, in-country and speaking the national language.
quote: it's difficult to find the right profile for this… going to have to have a link with systems transitioning, have to have a link on how the cluster is going to function in the future. So you really need someone that is embedded into the team and have a good understanding of Sudan. And that means being in Sudan, speaking Arabic. And we don't think we can find the right profile for the moment.

statement: A central reporting platform launched mid-year asks partners to upload projects retroactively from the start of the year, which is difficult alongside the reporting systems already in use.
quote: this is in this month, so the middle of the year, and then it's like starting the plan from the middle of the year

statement: Replacing cluster reporting with a central system changes beneficiary counting, indicators and data flow at once, and raises a question about where responsibility for defining how sector results are measured should sit..
quote: We really think that what OCHA is trying to propose is against the technical leadership of the cluster and is going to have an impact on the wash cluster of all cluster, but for the wash cluster on the reporting willingness for partners

statement: WASH beneficiary calculation is context-specific — a water yard serves a set number of people in one country and a different number elsewhere, and source types differ between contexts — so a single standardised reporting model risks misrepresenting what the sector delivered.
quote: The standard way of picking output, outcome, and indicator are not public health. They are water, they are sanitation and hygiene

statement: Where a cluster has a functioning reporting system, an interface bridging it to the central platform would avoid partners reporting twice while keeping the sector calculation with the people who understand it.
quote: we are not going to be able to use OCHA data

statement: Having a cluster coordinator in every one of the eighteen states, which no other cluster has, gives the sector enough technical standing to push back when fragmented parallel structures are proposed.
quote: we are a strong cluster at state level, because we are the only cluster that have 18 state cluster coordinator. So we have very strong leadership technically, and also nationally we are very strong. So it's quite, let's say, we managed to push back because we have the technical expertise.

statement: Some states moved to create a separate outbreak coordination platform with its own information management, which the cluster raised concerns about, given how many coordination structures are already in place.
quote: the fragmentation is still there. It's even worse in terms of in some states they wanted to create a cholera platform and they are doing starting to do cholera IM. So we're pushing back.

statement: Between sixty-five and seventy partners are registered nationally but more operate in practice, and state platforms carry their own partners who are not always connected to the national platform.
quote: We have almost like registered if you say 65, 70 partners, but there are more partners. There are a lot of partners which comes in different states. So we know in one state there may be a lot of partners which may not be connected to the national platforms. So state platforms have their own partners and sometimes they're connected, sometimes they are not connected.

statement: The most recent census predates the current crisis by close to a decade, so there is no reliable baseline against which needs can be measured.
quote: looking at the census survey, we are referring to a census survey, which is of 2016-18. So there is very difficult to have an established baseline which we can refer to.

statement: Outbreak coordination cannot be run nationally because epidemiological information is too fragmented to arrive in time, so it has to be organised state by state — in practice coordinating eighteen separate outbreaks with their own data, partners and supply chains.
quote: it's managing 18 states, it's managing 18 outbreaks actually, because they will have their own source of data, if they will have their own

statement: A weekly outbreak coordination training for state coordinators is being delivered alongside development of the guidance and tools it teaches, tailored to the context but potentially reusable elsewhere.
quote: we have been working on the training for state coordinators on outbreak coordination module… we do it every Thursday for three hours… In the meantime, with a small group we are developing the guidance and we are developing the tools.

statement: Rules on collecting location data differ between states, with coordinates permitted in some and prohibited in others, which constrains outbreak response planning.
quote: In West Cordovan, you cannot take GPS coordinates because it's not allowed. In Darfur, you can. So, you know, these kind of things that for cholera are very important.

statement: Water systems are repeatedly targeted in areas of active conflict, so service continuity is interrupted by attack as well as by funding or capacity.
quote: one of the typical things which happens here are drone attacks. These water systems are consistently attacked in the conflicting area where the ongoing fighting is going on… So they attack the water systems.

statement: The pooled fund prioritisation exercise required localities to be selected within forty-eight hours using a model the cluster had reservations about, on the understanding it could be refined later; in practice the initial selection has held for the year.
quote: They ask us to rush and define in 48 hours which localities, with a model that is terrible, saying that we will have time to refine and all that. Now we cannot refine now.

statement: Applying geographic prioritisation to emergency supplies works against the objective where needs are dispersed: prepositioned stock needs to reach any pocket of need, and outbreaks are now occurring in localities that were not prioritised and cannot be supplied.
quote: cholera is happening in some localities that have not been prioritized and I cannot send supplies

statement: A written explanation of the cluster's concerns with the prioritisation methodology did not change the approach for that allocation; an after-action review is now underway, which offers a route to revisit it.
notes: Extracted from Sudan country consultation. | UNVERIFIED 2026-08: quote backfill found no passage supporting a written explanation of the cluster concerns. The transcript covers the 48-hour deadline, the model, supplies not reaching unprioritised localities, and an after-action review survey — but nothing about a document being submitted. Second record of this kind after Haiti E0513. Check against the recording or delete.

statement: A single strategic outcome set at humanitarian coordinator level gives the allocation coherence, while leaving sector gaps that sit outside its scope still needing a funding route.
quote: the outcomes was health service continuity… Personally, I think it's good, because at least there is only one objective, we all work around it. However, there is big wash gaps that still need funding.

statement: The pooled fund grant management system offers outputs and indicators structured only around water, sanitation and hygiene, with no public health framing, which makes it difficult to frame an outbreak response within the reporting structure, and can direct otherwise appropriate activities to the wrong locations.
quote: they have only indicator on water sanitation and hygiene… The standard way of picking output, outcome, and indicator are not public health. They are water, they are sanitation and hygiene, so you don't have any means to actually develop a public health response

statement: Adding public health outcomes and indicators to pooled fund reporting structures would let outbreak response be planned and measured as transmission reduction rather than as separate water, sanitation and hygiene outputs.
quote: you don't have any means to actually develop a public health response

statement: Development and reconstruction finance from development banks is channelled through UN agencies because it cannot be given directly to government, creating a parallel and much larger funding stream alongside the humanitarian one.
quote: there's a whole lot of support coming from World Bank and AFDB, also KFW

statement: After a survey exposed water supply gaps, a bilateral donor funded six semi-decentralised systems designed to exit water trucking, with a joint cluster concept note, a steering committee overseeing installation, and explicit decisions on operating costs and whether management would be community-based or utility-run.
quote: there have been a lot of investment in Tawila, including in deploying supplies for semi-centralized systems. And we wanted a bit to see the impact of this.

statement: A six-month cluster report brings together response progress, coordination progress, financial status, the core supply pipeline, a facility assessment and partner case studies in a single product.
quote: you will receive the midterm report for the wash cluster. So we are doing a six months where we are, which include the response progress, the wash cluster progress, the financial status, but also the core pipeline that we have established

statement: A co-coordinating partner was selected through a published terms of reference, but a compliance concern paused the process, and the cluster is deciding whether to re-advertise or return to the original applicant list.
quote: we did a TOR and we selected a partner who was going to be in that role of a co-coordinator. And unfortunately, there was a red flag on this partner, and then we had to put everything on hold… whether there is probably a need to do another announcement and another selection of a partner or go back to the list of applicants

statement: An information management post was requested inside the line ministry so that government holds its own capacity, co-leads the function and helps define what the role covers ahead of the handover.
quote: We have requested through the Commissioner, who is the lead in the Ministry of Water Resources, a position of an IMO. So that the Information Management Officer sitting at the Ministry of Water Resources can, when selected, co-lead and also help in mapping out the tasks of an IMO

statement: The coordination link at local government level is not yet in place: departments and the state water agency need mentoring and coaching before they can carry coordination, even though national arrangements are agreed.
quote: there is need to strengthen the LGA level departments as well as [the state water agency], who is supposed to also be sitting and working under the Ministry of Water Resources, but they need a little bit of mentoring, coaching and strengthening so that that coordination link that is absent at the moment is brought into existence

statement: Rather than assuming what ministry capacity gaps are, the cluster commissioned a capacity gap analysis first, on the basis that describing capacity as weak says nothing about what support would actually help.
quote: we are talking about weaker capacities of the ministries, but we really do not know weak means what. So [the incoming coordinator], who has just recently joined us, is going to do an analysis, a capacity gap analysis. And based on that analysis, we'll be able to come back to you and say, these are the gaps that are existing.

statement: Connecting neighbouring countries facing the same cross-border outbreak through a shared space for materials and experience was proposed as a practical form of peer support.
quote: it can be helpful to connect you with your colleagues in Niger, in Chad, in Cameroon. Let us know. We can also make potentially a small teams group or something where different materials could be shared if that could be useful.

statement: One information management officer covers both the WASH and education sectors, so information management for each is delivered at partial capacity.
quote: I have two sections now supporting education and wash. So we'll see how we can organize the dashboard

statement: Transition to government-led coordination began at the start of the year, with the line ministry taking the lead supported by an NGO co-coordinator, on a timetable running to the end of the following year.
quote: the transition period commenced early this year in January… the transition as it is right now means that the Ministry of Water Resources takes lead. The arrangement and the leadership structure is such that we will have the ministry taking lead and having a co-coordinator who is an NGO to support that transition period. That transition period is until 2027 December.

statement: Training of trainers for state facilitators and co-coordinators had to be delivered remotely rather than in person because of funding constraints, before a five-day session with state representatives.
quote: this kind of training is done physically, but because of the funding gaps, she was not able to come here. So she did a TOT and then we ended up having a five day training with all the representatives from the three states.

statement: Ministry staff nominated to lead coordination do not yet hold the skill sets the role needs, and a five-month deployment was arranged to build them.
quote: that's where we have a little bit of gap in terms of existing capacities and skill sets within the ministry… [he] will be here for the next five months, probably with the possibility of an extension

statement: A state advisory group is to endorse the transition plan and provide continuing oversight, so that the arrangement is formalised within the ministry rather than resting on individual relationships.
quote: there will be a governance body, a state advisory group, which of course has to endorse this transition plan so that then they can provide ongoing oversight and make sure that this is formalized within the ministry

statement: Ministry staff taking on coordination need training on emergency preparedness and response planning, contingency planning and aligned monitoring tools, not only on coordination mechanics.
quote: They need to be trained on the EPR as well as the contingency planning, as well as aligned monitoring tools. And of course, as UNICEF, we are happy to provide that training

statement: The multi-sector needs assessment is led by a national NGO, which has run the country assessment programme for several years in place of an international assessment partner.
quote: by another organization here, we call it the [national] Foundation, a local NGO here, a national NGO that has been leading the assessment activities here. And they are the one that conducted the last MSNA in 2024.

statement: No wider multi-sector needs assessment was conducted last year, so the response plan rested on secondary data analysis alone.
quote: in 2025, last year, unfortunately, we don't have a wider MSNA rather than neither the sector specific assessment, which we will base our HNRP based on the secondary data analysis

statement: A large cholera outbreak is running concurrently with the transition, with cases declining in one urban area while rising in others, and the household-level response approach is not sufficient in the worst-affected locations.
quote: We are talking about almost 36,000 cases right now. Declining in areas of Maiduguri, but also we see an upward trend in places like Monguno… the CATI teams will not be able to just be focusing at house level. Probably we need to do cluster approach.

statement: The outbreak has a cross-border dimension with three neighbouring countries, and containment depends on coordination that no single country platform currently provides.
quote: there is also a cross-border issue at the border of Nigeria, Borno, as well as also Niger, Chad, and also Cameroon, because of many reasons… And we have to contain it. We have to stop this spreading.

statement: The technical working group leading the outbreak response is chaired by an international NGO rather than the lead agency, with the sector spanning all partner agencies and the ministry.
quote: the technical lead for the cholera technical working group is [an international NGO] person. And we have all these agencies within the sector with capacities to support the coordination. And then we have the ministry.

statement: Technical support to an outbreak should be pitched at the whole sector rather than routed through the lead agency alone, so that all partners work from the same guidance, tools and training.
quote: when we're thinking of cluster or sector coordination, that it goes a bit beyond UNICEF… we think other partners should also be using the same guidance, the same tools, benefit from the same training. So I just want to make sure when we're thinking about sector that we are going a bit wider than just UNICEF

statement: Coordination capacity during the transition is being provided through a standby partner deployment at no cost to the country office, which fills the gap but does not establish a funded post.
quote: for now, the coordination aspect is a standby partner. So you know what that means. We essentially are not paying anything.

statement: Key informants for the needs analysis were departmental water and sanitation directors, but almost all had just been rotated into new posts when the questionnaire went out, so responses were difficult to use and the gap had to be filled by a cluster workshop.
quote: on s'était basé sur les directions, les directeurs départementaux de l'hydraulique et de l'assainissement. Mais au moment même où on avait partagé le questionnaire, ils étaient pratiquement tous nouveaux parce qu'on avait fait des réaménagements pour affecter d'autres dans d'autres zones. Donc du coup, ils n'ont pas très bien compris le questionnaire, et on avait eu beaucoup de données qu'on n'a pas pu utiliser.

statement: The statistics directorate of the line ministry asked to join the cluster mailing list this year in order to receive cluster information, the first time government has sought the data directly.
quote: cette année en début d'année, la direction de la statistique de notre ministère de tutelle a demandé à intégrer les mailing lists du Cluster pour pouvoir recevoir les informations du Cluster… quand même, ils sont très intéressés à avoir les informations que nous collectons avec le cluster

statement: The cluster 5W sits on a platform built in-country and shared with other sectors; with a new central module also asking partners to report, it is unresolved whether partners should continue filling the cluster system, both, or neither.
quote: on a mis notre 5W, c'est une plateforme créée ici même au niveau local au Niger qui s'appelle [Statkite] et pratiquement les clusters nutrition, les clusters dont UNICEF est lead sont tous sur cette plateforme. C'est là-bas qu'on collectait nos 5W. Mais avec l'arrivée de ce module pays Activity Info où il demande aussi aux partenaires de rapporter, on a soulevé cette question.

statement: The cluster terms of reference were revised to cover current issues and a new thematic working group, but not area-based coordination, because the cluster was not approached about it.
quote: on a révisé pour intégrer les nouvelles questions qui sont en cours d'actualité, mais aussi le nouveau GT qu'il n'y avait pas dans notre terme de référence avant… Mais c'est pas pour intégrer les [ABC] parce que nous on n'a pas été contactés par rapport à ces [ABC].

statement: Gastroenteritis cases have been notified near the border with a neighbouring country where a large cholera outbreak is under way, and emergency preparations are being made with the zone offices.
quote: on a commencé à recevoir au Nigeria et on a eu des cas de gastro-entérite ici au Niger, à la frontière avec ce même Nigeria, donc y a des probabilités qu'il y ait aussi au Niger… Nous sommes dans les préparatifs d'une réponse d'urgence là pour des cas de gastro-entérite qui ont été notifiés dans la région de Diffa.

statement: Measured against a definition of area-based coordination operating at the smallest administrative unit, the country does not have it: a pilot covering four of two hundred and sixty-six communes was tried and did not continue beyond the pilot.
quote: on est à 266 communes, donc d'après ce que j'ai compris, ça va jusqu'au niveau communes normalement, c'est-à-dire que c'est la plus petite forme de coordination… donc si on se base sur cette définition, on peut dire qu'au Niger, on n'a pas cette [forme]. On avait eu seulement le flagship qui ressemblait à ça qu'on a voulu faire sur 4 communes et ça même ça n'a pas abouti.

statement: Treated instead as regional structures, five functional coordination groups meet monthly and work for practically all sectors — so whether the country has area-based coordination depends entirely on which administrative level the definition refers to.
quote: si on prend les régions comme des aires à base coordination, actuellement on a 5 GT qui sont fonctionnels et c'est des systèmes de coordination au niveau région qui se réunissent mensuellement. Donc si on prend la définition pour s'arrêter au niveau région, on peut dire que ça fonctionne pour pratiquement tous les clusters au Niger.

statement: An advocacy committee bringing together the cluster thematic sub-groups and members with advocacy expertise was recommended two years ago and has still not been established, because each year emergencies require the workplan to be reprioritised.
quote: il a été proposé d'avoir un comité de plaidoyer et ce comité doit réunir l'ensemble des sous-groupes thématiques du Cluster élargi à quelques membres qui ont vraiment l'expertise en plaidoyer. Mais on n'a pas pu mettre ça en place, c'est une recommandation qui était là depuis 2024 mais que jusque-là on n'arrive pas à mettre en place. Parce que chaque année y a des urgences et on est obligé de faire des priorités.

statement: A change to the pooled fund project review process arrived with a day’s notice and required the committee to meet across the week and nominate members for an in-person session, displacing the cluster meeting and other planned work.
quote: ce matin, des mails tombent où on nous demande de faire l'évaluation des projets… On pensait que c'est comme d'habitude, c'est le comité d'orientation stratégique ensemble qui va se réunir les 3 jours. Non, ils ont changé de stratégie cette année. Il demande au comité de se réunir aujourd'hui et demain pour évaluer les projets et de désigner 2 membres qui vont participer à la rencontre en présentiel… ça veut dire qu'ils vont nous consommer toute cette semaine.

statement: A donor delegation met the cluster to discuss strategic priorities and advised that proposals emphasise environmental impact assessment and the donor four environmental priority areas, which the cluster is now building into partner capacity building and its advocacy strategy.
quote: des experts d'ECHO qui sont venus au Niger en mission, qui ont voulu rencontrer le Cluster Wash pour discuter des priorités stratégiques pour cette année… Ils ont dit que surtout, surtout, c'est de mettre l'accent sur les études d'impact environnemental, la prise en compte de leurs 4 axes prioritaires en termes d'environnement.

statement: A database that takes data pasted from the cluster reporting platform and returns results by indicator has made routine information products quick to produce, and the cluster considers information management its strongest area.
quote: grâce à cette base de données où je copie seulement des données de notre plateforme de collecte de notre 5W pour coller dans la base de données et ça me fait sortir par indicateur… je peux dire que côté gestion de l'information on avance vraiment comme il le faut

statement: A discrepancy between the reporting platform and the dashboard affects the total people-reached figure, and reconciling the two requires support the cluster does not hold in-house.
quote: j'ai remarqué une petite différence… je vais te montrer la petite différence qu'il y a au niveau des feuilles, les résultats de ces feuilles, et ça a des conséquences sur le nombre de personnes atteintes globalement qui s'affichent sur notre dashboard

statement: The response to questions about which reporting system applies has been that the central module is a pilot and no answer is available yet, so partners have not begun reporting into it and the cluster continues extracting from its own platform alongside an interim spreadsheet.
quote: on a soulevé ça, ils ont dit puisque c'est un projet pilote. Pour le moment, personne n'a la solution. Donc qu'est-ce qu'ils font ? Ils nous partagent un fichier Excel où ils nous demandent de rapporter nos réalisations et nous on continue de tirer les réalisations sur la plateforme… rien n'est clair ici au Niger.

statement: A transition plan was raised once at an intersectoral meeting as something every cluster should have; the cluster asked how it should be done, received no answer, and has not been contacted since, so ordinary coordination continues with neither government nor partners raising it.
quote: vers la fin de l'année passée, on avait eu un call pendant une réunion à l'ICCG. Ils ont commencé à nous parler des transitions. Ils ont dit que normalement, tous les clusters doivent avoir un plan de [transition]. On avait dit oui, OK, mais comment ça doit se passer ? En tout cas, on n'a pas eu de réponse et jusque-là on ne nous a pas contactés par rapport à ces plans de transition.

statement: The cluster contributed indicators and questionnaire content to the planned multi-sector assessment and asked to take part in enumerator training, was told it would be included, and then heard nothing; collection was due to start in July and had not begun by mid-month.
quote: On a appris que REACH va faire la MSNA à travers [un partenaire] qui est ici au Niger. Donc on est allé jusqu'à travailler sur les indicateurs et le questionnaire. Après, ils ont dit qu'ils vont commencer les formations des enquêteurs. On a demandé à être impliqués dans la formation de ces enquêteurs… mais depuis lors [silence].

statement: With no multi-sector assessment last year, the cluster updated the previous one through key informants and agreed severity levels collectively at a cluster workshop.
quote: Y avait pas de MSNA mais on avait utilisé l'ancienne MSNA. On a fait juste les mises à jour avec les informateurs clés… on a complété avec un atelier du Cluster qui a réuni tous les [membres] et on a décidé [des seuils] de sévérité ensemble, mais si on pouvait avoir la MSNA, c'est plus facile que cette méthode.

statement: The coordinator and information manager posts are formally split half between coordination and programme, but both have worked at full time or beyond on coordination throughout the emergency, and the formal split is due to be reinstated.
quote: technically me and [the IM officer] are 50% capacity, other 50% should be on programme. But in the last four months of the emergency, that has not been the reality because of the workload, the amount of coordination IM needed in terms of the emergencies has meant that we've basically been like 100% or more for that

statement: Subnational coordination leads are NGO staff acting voluntarily on top of their own roles, and their organisations absorb the time; several are already overstretched.
quote: we've been extremely lucky with those NGOs that are working voluntarily as subnational leads, that their NGOs have given them so much time to work as a subnational lead… putting even more responsibility onto the shoulders of these voluntary NGOs in these different subnational areas, I think that's the last thing we should be doing at the moment because they're already overstretched as it is

statement: A coordination performance review should ask partners, organisations and ministries how the sector has functioned, rather than the coordination team assessing itself, so that the resulting evidence can support the case for what needs to change.
quote: if you ask every one of us how it's working, we will say it's working well. From my side, for example, it is working well, but I'm providing 200% of my time to have things being done. So the first thing that we need support from my side is to start a real CCPM to check exactly how for the past year the coordination was working… Not about asking us, but more about asking the partners, the organizations, the ministries

statement: Area coordination groups work in detail locally but there is no equivalent operational discussion at central level, so issues stay compartmentalised within each area rather than aggregating into a national picture.
quote: you have a really hands on [area group] in each area who want to go into the nitty gritty, like even why is there no bottled water in this village… and then it doesn't really go centralized. It just stays in there… because we don't have this technical discussion or this operational discussion actually at central level. It's very compartmentalized within each area.

statement: Water establishment capacity varies markedly between regions: one has an information management focal point working closely with the sector, while in another the post is paid for by the lead agency until the end of the year.
quote: For water establishments, it depends which one. In the south, they have quite good IM awareness and there is an IM focal point who works in the south and they work closely with the team… For [another region], UNICEF is paying for the IM person in the water establishment and that is going to last until the end of the year.

statement: Coordinators asked for documented cases, successful or not, of responsibility being handed to local actors, national NGOs or public utilities, in order to judge whether such arrangements hold in practice.
quote: for any kind of transition plans that have the idea of maybe the sector in general relinquishing responsibility to local actors or to national NGOs or to water boards like water establishments. If there's any other case studies, good or bad, like if there's any documentation on that, I would be really interested to read them just to gauge an idea of how these things have worked previously and if they actually ever work.

statement: Tools built during an earlier emergency — a site booking sheet for partners and a linked reporting database — were reusable from day one of the next one, so information management was ready even where the response was not.
quote: 2024 we have the tools and 2026 I just need to replicate the tools. So from day one we have the tools ready in terms of the booking sheet where a partner go and book which site they need to intervene in… linking it with the reporting database as well. The database was ready since 2024. We just need to replicate it. We learned from our mistakes.

statement: A transition plan shifting subnational responsibility to national NGOs and to public water establishments set a target that five months of emergency showed to be beyond what any of those actors could carry, and the plan is being reopened for revision.
quote: this last five months has sort of proven that that transition plan is too, let's say, the target is too high. It's a bit unrealistic. So we will have to get back over the next few weeks and the next month to really look into that transition plan and to evaluate it and see where we can amend it to make it a bit more realistic

statement: Under the transition design, water establishments were to chair subnational meetings and follow up referrals on the stabilisation side; in practice their participation in those meetings has been minimal.
quote: it was agreed that meetings would be ad hoc and that the two voluntary NGOs would take the humanitarian side of it and the water establishment would take the stabilization side of it. Even in terms of chairing meetings, even in terms of follow up with referrals with the water establishment, it was designed to be given, relinquishing those responsibilities to the water establishment. From my knowledge, that's never happened.

statement: International NGOs withdrew from subnational coordination during the emergency and the lead agency had to fund positions so that local NGOs could keep the structure running.
quote: We've had international NGOs pull out during the emergency of sub-national coordination, and UNICEF have had to fund positions for local NGOs to remain in the coordination. So there still is a huge reliance on UNICEF to keep this structure of this coordination going.

statement: Area coordination groups are formalised with the coordination office, with leadership allocated through an expression of interest for one UN agency and one NGO per area and rotated every three to four months.
quote: they're formalized with OCHA and they had an expression of interest per UN agency and per NGO in each area. And they do rotate them, I think, every three or four months

statement: Area groups vary considerably in how proactive they are, and some pursue positions at odds with their own central counterparts.
quote: some [area groups] are much more proactive and much more detail-oriented than the others. Like in the South, for example, they're very hands-on. They want to get things done now, even going against their central counterparts.

statement: The line ministry leads the sector formally but took a limited role during the emergency, attending central operations meetings only where sector-specific items were tabled, with a single focal point covering the workload of several.
quote: the Ministry of Energy and Water were probably the least involved ministry within the emergency… there was an operations room meeting where a lot of ministry representatives alongside the sector leads would have operational and strategic meetings maybe once or twice a week at central level. And unfortunately, Ministry of Energy and Water were not present once. They were only present in those meetings where there were specific wash discussions… [the focal point] herself is doing the job of four or five people.

statement: An arrangement placing a post half in the sector and half in the ministry reached three final candidates, but the ministry did not take up any of them.
quote: even giving them some additional staff capacity, maybe to have someone half sector, half ministry. We spoke of that, we tried that at the end of last year. But the ministry, we even had three final candidates, but the ministry didn't want any of them.

statement: Where rapid needs assessment required an approval that took time to obtain, the exercise was reframed as a rapid technical assessment focused on shelter conditions and standards, which allowed it to proceed and has now run three rounds.
quote: the rapid need assessment of the sites, going to the shelters, everything required approval before and sometimes approval take a lot of time. So we initiate an idea that I name it RTA, so Rapid Technical Assessment. And the reality is it's the same, it's a rapid need assessment, but we have to overcome the challenge… we have to explain it to the government lead that this is a technical assessment that will be very quick

statement: Linking the rapid assessment to the booking and reporting systems produced a measure of how quickly sites were responded to, by partner and for the sector as a whole, which then informed pooled fund allocation decisions.
quote: RTA, it's a full solution that was done from the assessment to the dashboard to show if we are meeting standards or not, and the linkage with other tools that we have, such as reporting. So from these three things, we create what's called the efficiency of the response… the response rate of every partner, the response rate of the sector.

statement: Maintaining the same data in several formats at once — dashboard and spreadsheet — accommodates partners with different technical capacities without splitting the underlying data.
quote: in different NGO you have different people, different positions, different mentalities. So some people like Power BI and know how they use dashboards. Others, they don't know. They are still using Excel and Google Sheets… we had different tools that all are linked together and all working at the same time, so to have the same data on Power BI, you will have the same data in the Google Sheet at the same time

statement: The multi-sector assessment does not reach nationwide coverage, and the areas excluded are among those most changed by the conflict, so the change in conditions is the part hardest to measure.
quote: some areas are not being covered, so they are not able to cover all like nationwide. And what I really care about is the areas that were really changed in terms of like the war affect these areas. We have a lot of areas that now they don't have access to water, they don't have access even to the markets, to the bottled water… So some of these areas are not being covered for MSNA.

statement: Two separate population assessments run in parallel covering different groups, and although the sector aligned the questions between them, merging the two has been discussed for a long time without resolution.
quote: Still, unfortunately, not harmonized… we have been discussing a long time about merging both. At our side as a sector, we try to harmonize the question to be aligned together. So, same questions here and there, but in terms of higher level, still the two different assessments.

statement: A national survey was published several years after collection and only at subnational level, and the ministry was not inclined to adopt the results, so its value for planning was limited.
